analysis.title: The Top-Down Investor – Chart(s) of the Month: A Top-Down Approach to The Debates Surrounding Semiconductors
key_insights: The S&P 500 Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment group is down about 31% from its June 2026 peak. It is still up 3% year-to-date (ex-dividends), 427% since 2022 and 2,663% since 2009, against 5%, 88% and 544% for the S&P 500.

The current drawdown is the ninth-largest in the sector's history. Past drawdowns cluster in the 30%-50% range: 2022 (-49%), 1990 (-42%), the 2026 Iran war (-39%), 1996 and 1998 (-38% and -37%), Covid 2020 (-35%) and the 2025 tariff sell-off (-35%). The dot-com bust was the worst at -86%. A few more points of decline would put this one among the most severe.

Silicon wafer shipments rose 13.4% YoY in 3Q26, up from 7.4% in 2Q26, led by AI. HBM, advanced DRAM and AI accelerators lead, while conventional memory recovers slowly and analog, power and industrial chips stay weak. Revenue growth outruns volume growth because of higher memory prices and a richer product mix.

The cycle is polarized. Global PC shipments fell 20.1% YoY in 3Q26, smartphone shipments are expected to fall 16.7% in 2026 (27.2% in 2H26), and AI server shipments are expected to grow about 31% in 2026. Higher memory prices are hurting consumer electronics demand, so the upcycle depends on continued AI infrastructure spending.

South Korean semiconductor exports remain strong, driven by AI demand, memory prices and mix rather than an equivalent rise in volumes. The latest data shows some moderation in price inflation and volumes at a more stable level.

Hyperscaler capex growth is expected to slow to 47% in 2027 from 93% in 2026. Consensus semiconductor EPS growth already appears to reflect this slowdown, but slowing capex, high operating leverage, higher chip prices and capacity expansion raise doubts about the sustainability of earnings expectations.

Additional uncertainty comes from the 'Blue Wave' in the US midterms, which adds to concerns about hyperscaler capex execution, from the recent CEO change at Nvidia, and from concerns about potential export-control violations and their legal implications. Santander says risks to consensus earnings may be larger than the capex slowdown alone implies.

Price performance has historically led EPS growth, but a divergence has opened between sector prices and consensus earnings growth. Consensus has margins staying near historically elevated levels until at least 2028, the last year hyperscaler capex growth is projected to stay comfortably in double digits. The risk lies beyond 2028 if demand slows or turns negative while capacity keeps expanding.

Earnings revisions are still positive but fading. Large upward revisions between 2H25 and 1H26 lifted expected growth, but since then revisions have been more moderate and have not changed the expected trajectory of the earnings cycle.

Valuations are historically low. 12-month forward P/E is about 23% below the 2006-2019 average (ex-2009) and 39% below the 2006-YTD average. 24-month forward P/E of 8.3x is the lowest since 2006, below the 2011 summer lows, and implies a return toward 2018-2022 net margin levels.

Positioning has not capitulated. Almost three-quarters of YTD semiconductor ETF inflows came after the summer peak, and inflows continued through the sell-off that began in early October. Recent daily flows suggest the trend may be weakening, though there were still marginal inflows on October 19.

Santander keeps a Neutral stance on the semiconductor complex. It was underweight EM Asia and overweight the US in the summer, and partially reversed that preference in its recent Asset Allocation Review. Its Europe and LatAm positioning leaves it slightly underweight semiconductors on a relative basis.

Santander wants clearer evidence of an unwinding of investor positioning before turning significantly more constructive. It also says a further price correction, potentially in the high-single-digit range, would bring the drawdown closer to previous major sell-offs.

sector_views.rationale: Falling prices and low valuations make the sector more attractive, but investor positioning shows no clear capitulation and revisions are fading. Santander stays Neutral for now.

earnings_insights: Consensus (estimate, not reported) has US semiconductor net margins staying close to historically elevated levels at least until 2028. Santander says current multiples increasingly discount a return to the 2018-2022 net margin levels.

Consensus estimates already appear to reflect the expected slowdown in hyperscaler capex growth to 47% in 2027 from 93% in 2026. Santander sees risks to consensus semiconductor earnings as potentially larger than that slowdown alone implies.
Positive EPS revisions continue at a more moderate pace than between 2H25 and 1H26 and have not materially changed the expected trajectory of the earnings cycle.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 7.4% in 2Q26, driven mainly by AI demand. Physical volume growth is more moderate than the surge in semiconductor revenues.
Rising memory costs and higher retail prices weigh on consumer electronics demand.
Contraction in consumer devices contrasts with AI-driven demand for server chips.
AI investment is the main support for the semiconductor upcycle.
The rate of capex growth is turning down sharply, though levels are still rising.

risk_factors: Slowing hyperscaler capex growth (47% in 2027 vs 93% in 2026) combined with high operating leverage and capacity expansion could pressure earnings expectations.
Net margins could fall after 2028 if demand growth slows or turns negative while production capacity keeps expanding.
Governance issues at Nvidia, including the CEO change and export-control concerns, and a potential tightening of export restrictions to China.
US midterm election outcome ('Blue Wave') adding to concerns about AI infrastructure deployment.
Consumer electronics demand is weakened by higher memory prices, with PC and smartphone shipments contracting.
Further downward earnings revisions could undermine the apparent valuation attractiveness.
Unwinding of crowded semiconductor ETF positioning could extend the sell-off.
vol_and_positioning: Almost three-quarters of YTD inflows into semiconductor equity ETFs came after the summer price peak, and investors kept buying through the sell-off that began in early October.
Recent daily ETF flow data suggest the buy-the-dip trend may be starting to weaken, though the October 19 sell-off still saw marginal inflows.
Santander sees no clear signs of capitulation or positioning unwind yet, which is the missing condition for a more constructive stance.
geopolitical: The 2026 outbreak of the Iran war coincided with a 39% semiconductor sector drawdown earlier in 2026.
The 'Blue Wave' in the recent US midterm elections adds to concerns about execution of hyperscaler AI infrastructure capex plans.
Potential tightening of export restrictions on US-related semiconductors to China is cited as a driver of the recent de-rating.
Concerns about potential export-control violations by Nvidia and their legal implications.

tension_points.bull_case: Forward P/E is 23% below its 2006-2019 average on 12-month earnings, and the 24-month multiple of 8.3x is the lowest since 2006, so the market already discounts a significant deterioration in forward earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Slowing capex growth, high operating leverage and capacity expansion could pressure margins beyond 2028, and further downward revisions could undermine the apparent attractiveness of low multiples.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A return of net margins to the 2018-2022 levels that current multiples increasingly discount would make the bull case redundant, and downward EPS revisions would break it. Santander says clearer evidence of a positioning unwind is also needed before turning constructive.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex expectations have continued to trend upwards, and the 2027 slowdown to 47% growth appears already reflected in consensus semiconductor EPS growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex growth falls from 93% to 47% while chip prices and capacity rise, and the midterm 'Blue Wave' adds execution concerns, so risks to consensus earnings may exceed the slowdown alone.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex growth turning negative while production capacity keeps expanding after 2028, which would put significant pressure on semiconductor margins.

tension_points.bull_case: Investors keep allocating to semiconductor ETFs through the sell-off, a buy-the-dip pattern consistent with broader equity markets.
tension_points.bear_case: Positioning has not capitulated, and recent daily flows suggest the trend may be starting to weaken.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A clear unwinding of investor positioning, together with a further price correction potentially in the high-single-digit range, would change Santander's Neutral stance.
